KEY INSIGHTS

Scale is meaningful, but growth quality has clear management risks.

The project does not treat topline marketplace size as sufficient evidence of health. The strongest decision signals sit in measurement quality, seller concentration, seller activation and delivery-related customer experience.

1

Measurement boundary matters

Executive-complete reporting ends 31 Aug 2018. The sparse Sep–Oct tail is not decision-eligible for trend interpretation.

2

High seller concentration

The top 20% of positive-GMV sellers contribute 82.7% of seller GMV proxy; Gini = 0.792.

3

Activation is a bottleneck

Only 15.8% of observable closed sellers activate within 30 days; 90-day activation reaches 42.1%.

4

Operational risk is material

Late orders show a +44.8pp low-review risk gap and a 5.87× observed risk ratio versus on-time orders.

Key Business Recommendations

◉

Govern acquisition quality

Use volume, conversion, downstream seller value, activation and retention together instead of ranking channels from one funnel rate.

◈

Improve seller activation

Instrument 7/30/60-day onboarding checkpoints and test interventions against retention and downstream value.

▤

Reduce operational risk

Prioritize delivery investigations by order volume × delay severity × review penalty.

◎

Monitor concentration

Track top seller shares and investigate high-value categories where seller breadth is fragile.

DEEP-DIVE ANALYSIS

The dashboard is the evidence layer. The sections below explain the analytical logic.

Each deep dive keeps the same management discipline: define the decision question, use the correct denominator and grain, quantify magnitude, state uncertainty, and avoid causal claims the data cannot support.

MARKETPLACE HEALTH

Breadth and productivity do not move together.

The final complete period adds sellers and orders, while value per transaction weakens. Marketplace growth therefore has to be decomposed rather than summarized with a single topline label.

SELLER ACQUISITION

Observed conversion differs by origin, but conversion alone does not identify the best channel.

Across 8,000 Marketing Qualified Leads (MQLs), origin is associated with conversion. Paid Search converts at 12.3%, Organic Search at 11.8%, and Social at 5.6%. Cramér’s V = 0.131 indicates a detectable but modest relationship.

Channel governance rule

Use a scorecard that links MQL volume → conversion → matched-seller value → activation → M3 retention guardrail. The “unknown” origin remains context only and should not be presented as a channel winner.

ACTIVATION & RETENTION

Seller time-to-value is slow after conversion.

Canonical v3 uses observable-window denominators. Censored sellers remain visible instead of being mislabeled as activation failures.

Canonical activation windows

15.8%30D · 130/825
30.8%60D · 247/803
42.1%90D · 324/769
44.3dobserved activator median

The 44.3-day figure is the median among observed activators, not a survival-estimated median. Retention by acquisition origin remains too imprecise to support a winner and is therefore used as a guardrail.

COMMERCIAL RESILIENCE

Marketplace value is highly concentrated.

Seller count alone overstates diversification. The top 20% of positive-GMV sellers generate 82.7% of seller GMV proxy and the Gini coefficient is 0.792.

Decision boundary

Concentration is a monitoring signal, not automatic proof that generic seller diversification will improve outcomes. Category economics, seller breadth and service quality must be considered together.

CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE & OPERATIONS

Late delivery is strongly associated with weaker review outcomes.

Among reviewed delivered orders, late orders average 2.57 review points versus 4.29 for on-time orders. Their low-review rate is 54.0% versus 9.2%.

+44.8pp

Observed low-review risk gap

The observed risk ratio is 5.87×. In an adjusted Generalized Linear Model (GLM), each additional delay day has an odds ratio of about 1.080 for a low review after controlling for category, customer state, order value, freight ratio and purchase month.

Interpretation

Association does not prove causality. Category, route, carrier, seller mix, review selection and other unobserved factors can still matter.

METHODOLOGY & GOVERNANCE

The analytical contract behind the report.

The project is designed so that measurement rules are established before management claims are made.

Grain-safe model

GMV stays at item grain before one-to-many joins. Delivery and review analysis stays at order grain.

Decision-eligible periods

Incomplete edge periods are excluded or explicitly flagged before trend interpretation.

Eligibility-aware activation

Fixed-window activation rates only use sellers observable for the complete 30/60/90-day window.

Retention observability

M3 retention excludes cohorts too young to observe and avoids ranking origins when confidence intervals overlap materially.

Statistical rigor

Confidence intervals, bootstrap evidence, False Discovery Rate (FDR) adjustment and an adjusted GLM support the descriptive layer.

Claim governance

Historical observational evidence is kept separate from causal conclusions and current-market claims.

Interpretation boundary

This is a historical anonymized Olist case study. GMV is a proxy rather than platform revenue or profit. Marketing cost is unavailable, so Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) are not estimated. Current production decisions would require refreshed data and controlled follow-up tests.
